verdict.label: not_comparable
verdict.rationale: Both abstracts report an inverse association between circulating irisin and fasting plasma glucose, but the populations differ fundamentally: study A examines adult T2DM patients (mean adult cohort with diabetes), while study B examines healthy Taiwanese schoolchildren aged 10.3 ± 1.5 years. The age and metabolic-health gap is a decisive comparability obstacle for a biomarker-physiology association, so the pair is not comparable despite the shared directional finding.

source_evidence.quote: The study analyzed the roles of circulating omentin-1 and irisin in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) concomitant with metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD).
There were 376 children (179 boys and 197 girls), aged 10.3 ± 1.5 years, were enrolled.

diagnostics.notes: Extraction on both sides is faithful: A extracts the inverse irisin-FPG association in T2DM patients (sentence 4, direction '-'), B extracts the inverse irisin-FPG association in boys adjusted for age (sentence 7, direction '-', P=.006). The underlying findings share direction, but the populations (adults with T2DM vs. healthy children) are too dissimilar for a meaningful comparison of this biomarker association.
